::: {.manual-status}
**Resource status:** Usable broad-beta. Select columns that expose distinctions relevant to your question. A matrix supports comparison; it is not itself a quality appraisal or synthesis.
:::

## Blank matrix

**Question or claim being examined:** [ ]
**Inclusion boundary:** [ ]

| Source ID | Context or population | Construct or question | Design or argument | Relevant evidence | Limitations or uncertainty | Supports, qualifies or challenges? | Exact source location |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [ ] | [ ] | [ ] | [ ] | [ ] | [ ] | [ ] | [ ] |

Add method-specific fields only when they will affect comparison: intervention, comparator, outcome and follow-up; theory and mechanism; archive and period; standpoint and interpretive frame; or data source and analytic approach.

## Completed example

**Question:** Under what conditions is research feedback actionable?

| Source ID | Context | Construct | Design | Relevant evidence | Boundary | Relationship | Location |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| HT07 | broad education | feedback information | review and model | goals, current performance and next action are distinguished | not doctorate-specific | supports mechanism | model section |
| WZ20 | education | feedback effects | meta-analysis | effects are heterogeneous and information content matters | varied educational settings | qualifies universal benefit claim | results and discussion |
| Local-01 | one doctoral programme | supervisory feedback experience | qualitative interviews | delayed comments were difficult to act on near milestones | small local sample | adds context and timing | participant-theme table |

**Provisional pattern:** actionability appears to depend on information and timing, but doctorate-specific evidence is thinner than the broad education literature.

**Contrary or missing evidence:** supervisory workload, disciplinary writing conventions, non-written feedback and evidence from remote or practice-based doctorates.

## Scenario test

Two studies report opposite findings. Before calling them contradictory, compare constructs, samples, settings, time points and analytical choices. If one studies immediate satisfaction and the other later performance, place them in different outcome columns. The disagreement may be apparent rather than substantive.
